Biology 2011-I.subject: Biology
Biology 2011-I.question: Due to contraction of eyeball, a long-sighted eye can see only
options: farther objects which is corrected by using convex lens
farther objects which is corrected by using concave lens
nearer objects which is corrected by using convex lens
nearer objects which is corrected by using concave lens
Biology 2011-I.answer: farther objects which is corrected by using convex lens
Biology 2011-I.explanation: (a)  The contraction of eyeball brings about in a long- sighted eye. To see the nearby objects, a convex lense is used.

Biology 2011-I.subject: Biology
Biology 2011-I.question: Insects that can transmit diseases to human are referred to as
Biology 2011-I.explanation: (c)  Insects that transmit diseases to humans are known as vectors. Insects may carry infection mechanically on feet or mouth parts, by passage through the digestive tract but without the insect being infected or by becoming an intermediate host with some part of the parasite’s life cycle occuring in the insect tissue.

Biology 2011-I.subject: Biology
Biology 2011-I.question: Which  one  among  the  following  industries produces the most non-biodegradable wastes?
Biology 2011-I.explanation: (a) The most non biodegradable wastes are produced by thermal power plants. They utilize radioactive elements as raw material and thus evolves radioactive wastes which takes a very long period (hundreds of years) for losing its radioactivity completely.

Biology 2011-I.subject: Biology
Biology 2011-I.question: In dry regions, the leaf size of a tree becomes smaller. It is so to
Biology 2011-I.explanation: (b)  The small leaves possess no or very few stomata thus the loss of water by transpiration is decreased and protects the plant from dehydration.

Biology 2011-I.subject: Biology
Biology 2011-I.question: Bats can fly in dark because they
Biology 2011-I.explanation: (c)  Bats can fly  in dark because they transmit ultrasonic waves. The bats have very poor vision. It cannot see in dark. It produces ultrasonic waves striking with the obstacles present on its path. The bat receives its echo and changes its path to protect itself from collision.

Biology 2011-I.subject: Biology
Biology 2011-I.question: White blood cells act
options: as a medium for oxygen transport from lungs to tissues
Biology 2011-I.explanation: (a)  White blood cells destroy foreign proteins (bodies) e.g pathogens by the process of phagocytosis and in this way protects the body from infection.

Biology 2011-I.subject: Biology
Biology 2011-I.question: Which one among the following elements/ions is essential in small quantities for the development of healthy teeth but causes mottling of the teeth if consumed in higher quantities?
Biology 2011-I.explanation: (c)  Fluoride is essential in small quantity for the protection of  the teeth but in high quantity it causes fluorosis deforming the teeth.

Biology 2011-I.question: When we eat something we like, our mouth waters. This is actually not water but fluid secreted from
Biology 2011-I.explanation: (c)  Salivary glands secrete amylase enzyme (ptyalin) and water to moist the food and to digest starch.  When we see, smell or eat something we like, the salivary glands are stimulated and secrete saliva in buccal cavity thus watering the mouth.

Biology 2011-I.subject: Biology
Biology 2011-I.question: Why do you feel cool under a tree but not so under a tin shed on a sunny day?
options: The greenness of the tree gives the cool feeling
The leaves convert water vapours into water which is a heat-absorbing process
The leaves give out water which vapourises absorbing some heat as latent heat
Biology 2011-I.answer: The leaves give out water which vapourises absorbing some heat as latent heat
Biology 2011-I.explanation: (d)  The transpiration takes place from the leaves surface all the time. The water taken out from leaves absorbs heat from the surrounding atmosphere to vapourise so the area under a tree becomes cool.
